the design and development of novel, high sensitivity optical interferometric sensors.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the feasibility of using coherence to reduce the sensitivity of optical interferometers to thermal noise.
the thermal noise in optical interferometers can be compensated by the coherence for underlying stochastic processes.
we have shown that thermal noise can be compensated in a Michelson interferometer by using coherence for the surface displacement and the surface strain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sensitivity to thermal phase fluctuations is reduced when a mirror is coated with a thin dielectric layer.
the phase upon reflection from an optical surface is a random variable that can be described by a Gaussian probability density function.
the sensitivity of the phase upon reflection to thermal fluctuations of a mirror is proportional to the square of the correlation length of fluctuations of the mirror's surface.
